title: The Dog Night, 2013
logline: Fourteen years. He doesn't set the dog down. He holds him the whole time. The dog looks at the dumpster from his arms.

panels.composition: The dumpster, bulb, night, exact. WOOD standing, holding BARNABY. Not setting him down.

image.prompt: a man standing behind a bowling alley at night holding an old dog in his arms before a rusted dumpster under a bulb, not setting him down, clean ink, no words

panels.composition: The dog, from Wood's arms, looking at the dumpster. Fourteen. The eyes mostly cloud.

image.prompt: close-up of a very old dog with clouded eyes looking calmly at something from a man's arms, no words

panels.composition: Wood's chin on the dog's head.

image.prompt: a man with his chin resting on the head of the old dog he holds, bulb light, no words

panels.composition: The sign. Three letters dark now. He walks under it with the dog and doesn't look up.

image.prompt: a man carrying an old dog beneath a bowling-alley neon sign with three letters gone dark, not looking up, night, clean ink with one spot tone, no words
image.notes: Three dark. The last Dog Night with Barnaby.

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: The last Dog Night with Barnaby. Held the whole time. Three letters dark.
